clue.text: Fanatical minority concealing guilt in France

indicators.note: concealing means disguising, so the letters of guilt in France are hidden under a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A band of zealots is hiding some shameful secret over in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' is the anagram signal here: the thirteen letters of GUILT IN FRANCE are disguised by rearrangement. 'in France' looks like a location but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the extreme fringe of a movement, a small band of zealots whose views go well beyond the mainstream.

clue.text: Like some flyers' frivolous manner when crossing Tehran, perhaps

indicators.note: crossing means the frivolous manner stretches across, holding the scrambled city inside

parts.note: frivolous means light, not serious
an air is a manner or bearing

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the city name is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A breezy pilot's flippant attitude while flying over the Iranian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the anagram of the city's name and 'when crossing' the container. 'flyers' are balloons and airships, not people, and the apostrophe belongs only to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Balloons and airships float because they are less dense than the atmosphere around them.

clue.text: They may turn up disdainfully to identify informers

definitions.meaning: people turn up their snouts in scorn
a nose is slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: Snooty faces are used to pick out the grasses in the gang.
explanation.walkthrough: A nose is slang for a police informer or spy; 'to identify' just links the readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobs tilt their snouts upward in scorn, and police slang calls a spy or informant by the same name.

clue.text: Half of them studied in the nude, or wearing ragged clothes

indicators.note: Half of takes the first two of the four letters of them

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
naked means bare

explanation.surface: Half the class studied life drawing from a nude model, or else dressed in rags.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'read' a subject is British for studying it at university. 'or' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn so thin that the weave shows, said of clothes or of the shabby person dressed in them.

clue.text: Extremely risky topic distressed an islander

indicators.note: distressed suggests damage, so the letters are knocked into a new order
Extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of risky

explanation.surface: A touchy subject has upset someone from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives RY, the first and last letters of 'risky'; 'distressed' rearranges RY + TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Mediterranean island republic of Cyprus.

clue.text: Conservative diverging from centre without advocating reform

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for diverging from centre goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: radial lines spread out from a central point

explanation.surface: A Tory drifting from the political middle ground who refuses to back change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'not' but means outside: RADIAL around C. The definition reads 'advocating reform', not its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring thorough or sweeping political change, going to the roots of a system.

clue.text: Subtle husband abandons comfortable position

indicators.note: abandons means the husband leaves, taking his letter out of the word

parts.note: a niche is a comfortable or suitable position

explanation.surface: A husband quietly gives up his cosy berth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' drops H (husband) from NICHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nice distinction is a fine, delicate one, the older sense of precise or fastidious.

clue.text: Joining a lot of elderly people in rent manoeuvre

indicators.note: in places the trimmed pensioners inside the rearranged letters
manoeuvre suggests moving things about, so the word rent is rearranged
a lot of means most but not all of the phrase, losing one letter

parts.note: old men are elderly people

explanation.surface: Pensioners joining a protest over a scheme to raise rents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' signals the anagram, 'a lot of' drops the last letter of the phrase, and 'in' sets the shortened phrase inside. 'Joining' is the noun sense, a signing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up as a member of a club, course or register is the act of becoming part of it.

clue.text: Agreement in the post

definitions.meaning: a match or ... between things that fit together
letters sent and received by mail

explanation.surface: A deal has been sent off by mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only links the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a close match between things and the letters exchanged by mail.

clue.text: Sluggish type returning party flag without backing Left

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other
returning tells us the words for party and flag are written backwards together

parts.note: a do is a party
to flag is to sag, to droop with tiredness

indicators.note: backing says the word for Left is set down in reverse

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A lazy sort turns back from a party, flagging, with no support from the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' and 'backing' both signal reversals, and 'without' means outside. 'Sluggish type' looks like a lazy person but is a playful nod to slugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slugs and snails belong to the mollusc class of gastropods, so a sluggish type is literally slug-like.

clue.text: A collector may have one — a French priest nearly ten

indicators.note: nearly means the word for the French priest stops short of its final letter

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, making ten

explanation.surface: Some cryptic arithmetic: a French clergyman is almost worth ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims the E from CURE, leaving CUR. IO is the crossword convention of reading 10 as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a small rare or curious object, the sort of thing people collect and display.

clue.text: Opera bill. "The Drunkard's Return"

indicators.note: Return, read as a reversal signal, sends the words for bill and drunkard back to front together

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A playbill advertising a melodrama called The Drunkard's Return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like part of a play's title but turns AC + SOT into TOSCA. AC (account) is a common abbreviation for a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera about the singer Floria Tosca, set in Rome in 1800, is one of the best-known works in the repertoire.

clue.text: Sea-girt territory where short measure is given

definitions.meaning: a Scottish word for a small island, land surrounded by sea
a small unit of length, one twelfth of a foot

explanation.surface: An island where drinkers are given short measure at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a small island is called an inch (as in Inchcolm); 'where ... is given' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots use the word for small islands like Inchkeith, and it is also the imperial unit of length, a fraction of a foot.

clue.text: Endless noisy drinking causing affront

indicators.note: Endless means the word for noisy drinking loses its final letter

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily

explanation.surface: Someone's loud, unending boozing gives offence to the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the P from SLURP. 'causing' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insult or slight, a remark that gives offence.

clue.text: Safe of tried strength, impervious to noise

parts.note: safe and sound: sound means unharmed, secure
proof describes something tested and found strong, as in armour

explanation.surface: A strongbox of proven toughness that also muffles sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like a strongbox but is the adjective, as in 'safe and sound'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated so that noise cannot pass through, like a recording studio.

clue.text: Nomadic tribe crossing a river for food

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged tribe straddles the other letters, holding them inside
Nomadic suggests letters wandering, so the word tribe is rearranged

explanation.surface: A wandering people ford a river in search of something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nomadic' makes REBIT from TRIBE; 'crossing' puts A + R inside it after the first R. Rarebit (Welsh rabbit) is cheese melted on toast, a British snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury dish of seasoned melted cheese poured over toast.

clue.text: Dear sounding drink consumed by social workers?

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
in, as in eaten in or taken in
ants are social insects, and many are workers

explanation.surface: Liquor is downed by care workers on a modest salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear sounding' means like the homophone 'deer', cud-chewing animals; 'social workers?' suggests carers but means ants.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer are cud-chewing animals, so creatures of that sort belong to the cud-chewers.

clue.text: One with pride in Sir Tristram's birthplace, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the place name is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: Lyonesse is the legendary land off Cornwall where the Arthurian knight Tristram was born

explanation.surface: A question about someone proud of hailing from the Arthurian hero's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with pride' suggests a proud person but means a member of a pride of lions; Lyonesse, Tristram's mythical lost land, sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions is called a pride, and the female hunters are its core members.

clue.text: Rome is ravaged in this Roman epic

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the Latin word

parts.note: hic is Latin, the Romans' language, for this

indicators.note: ravaged means the word Rome is laid waste and its letters scrambled

explanation.surface: A tale of the sack of the Eternal City told as a Latin epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ravaged' makes OMER from ROME, which goes 'in' HIC, Latin for 'this'. 'Roman' looks like part of the definition but marks the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and heroic in scale, like the Iliad and Odyssey attributed to the Greek poet of antiquity.

clue.text: Criminal swindle involved climbing equipment

indicators.note: involved means wrapped around, so the criminal surrounds the swindle

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a ramp is British slang for a swindle

explanation.surface: A crook's scam centred on mountaineering gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' signals the container. Ramp is old British slang for a swindle, and 'Criminal' is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiked metal frame strapped to a boot for gripping ice when mountaineering.

clue.text: Woman abstainer takes round orange

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name
TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A woman who never drinks reaches for an orange.
explanation.walkthrough: TT (teetotal) is the crossword convention for an abstainer; 'takes' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The seeds of a tropical tree yield a reddish-orange dye used to colour cheese and butter, so the dye names the colour.

clue.text: Old Christian centre — a name I observed in Talbot House

indicators.note: observed in means the letter is seen within the other word

parts.note: Toc H is the signallers' name for Talbot House, the soldiers' Christian club founded at Poperinge in 1915

explanation.surface: Someone spots a name on the wall of a famous soldiers' rest house.
explanation.walkthrough: TOC H, signallers' spelling of TH, names Talbot House, a First World War soldiers' club that became a Christian charity. Antioch was an early centre of the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Syrian city was where followers of Jesus were first called Christians.

clue.text: A number beginning to negotiate in the Orient

annotationWithheld.why: A number beginning to negotiate in the Orient (4): NO (number) + N (beginning to negotiate) + E (the Orient) builds the letters, but no clue word is left to define NONE
annotationWithheld.clue: A number beginning to negotiate in the Orient

clue.text: Shed made of metal

definitions.meaning: to shed is to throw off, as a snake does its skin
formed by pouring molten metal into a mould, as in iron objects

explanation.surface: A garden shed built out of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a noun (a hut) but is the verb: a snake casts its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw off a skin is to slough it; a metal object poured into a mould is a moulded one, as in iron goods.

clue.text: Remitted about a pound for tartan cloth

indicators.note: about means the word for remitted goes around the abbreviation for a pound

parts.note: a bill remitted has been settled, paid
L, from the Latin libra, is the sign for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone has paid roughly a pound for some tartan fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'roughly' but puts L inside PAID, after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen twilled cloth with a checked Scottish pattern, worn as a shawl over the shoulder in Highland dress.

clue.text: Like a bird following a Roman road north

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: Like a bird flying along an old Roman road towards the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or resembling birds, as in avian flu.

clue.text: Wrong set-up for this contracted revolutionary

indicators.note: set-up in a down clue means the word is lifted upwards, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A frame-up wrongly pinned on a jailed radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' suggests a frame but reverses TORT in this down clue. 'for this' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened name for a Trotskyist, a follower of the Russian revolutionary Leon Trotsky.

clue.text: Shot mine host? Keep away!

definitions.meaning: in target shooting, a shot landing in the ring next to the bull
a jocular reading as one belonging to the inn, the landlord, while Keep away playfully urges staying in rather than out

explanation.surface: Someone shot the landlord, and bystanders are warned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine host' is an old jocular name for a publican; the second reading treats the answer as 'one of the inn'.
explanation.definitionFit: A target's ring just outside the bull scores a hit of that name, and the landlord who keeps an inn is jokingly its man.

clue.text: Publicizing of concert by sea, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear signals the words for concert and sea are said aloud as another word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, and the sea is the ocean

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a seaside concert is being advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: PROM + OCEAN spoken quickly gives the sound of the answer; 'of' only links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising a product or event to raise its public profile is a campaign of that name.

clue.text: Put down the receiver to avoid committing oneself

parts.note: to sit on something is to suppress or put it down
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Hanging up the telephone to dodge making a commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' suggests a telephone handset but means a fence, a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means staying neutral and refusing to take either side in a dispute.
